question: Apple's diluted EPS grew faster (22.7%) than its net income (19.5%) from FY2024 to FY2025. What explains the gap?
answer: Apple’s diluted EPS grew faster because the diluted share count fell, reducing the denominator. Diluted shares dropped from 15,408,095 thousand in FY2024 to 15,004,697 thousand in FY2025 (~2.6% decline) [1]. Net income rose 19.5% from $93,736 million to $112,010 million [S3][S4], while diluted EPS rose 22.7% from $6.08 to $7.46 per share [S1][S2]. The lower share count amplified EPS growth relative to net income.
